epithet

EP-uh-thet -- from Greek epi- ('upon, in addition') + tithenai ('to place, put'). · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Epithet is descriptive nickname or label.

Journalists began attaching the epithet 'the Iron Duke' to the general after his fourth consecutive victory.

Example

After a pitcher throws a perfect game, sportswriters start calling him by the epithet 'Iceman' in every headline for the rest of the season.

An epithet is exactly that kind of descriptive nickname, attached to a name because it captures something notable about the person.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

sobriquet: A sobriquet is a nickname with a playful or affectionate flavor, often given with a wink -- a beloved jazz singer billed as 'Lady Day.' An epithet usually leans the other way: it is a respectful or descriptive title fastened to a name, like 'Alexander the Great,' recording something notable rather than teasing.

pet name: A pet name is a private, affectionate name used by the people closest to you -- 'Sunshine,' 'Bean' -- and it says more about the relationship than about the person. An epithet is public and descriptive: writers and historians attach it to a name because it captures a notable trait.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

anonymity: the state of being unknown or unnamed

obscurity: the state of being unknown or forgotten

Where it sits · how much the nickname says about someone — moniker → epithet → byword

moniker vs. epithet: Moniker is the casual end of the scale -- almost any nickname, however plain, can be a moniker, while an epithet captures something specific and notable about the person it names.

byword vs. epithet: Byword goes a step beyond epithet -- an epithet attaches a telling description to someone's name, while a byword is what a name becomes when it stands, all by itself, for a whole quality like cruelty or generosity.

The pieces

prefix — epi-

root — -thet-

Put it together

Put it together: Epithet comes from Greek epi- ('upon, in addition') plus tithenai ('to place, put') -- so an epithet is literally something 'placed upon' a name, a descriptive label attached to identify or characterize a person.

Word Choice

Epithet most often names a respectful or descriptive nickname, especially a historical one like 'Alexander the Great,' though informally the word is sometimes used for an insulting label instead -- context usually makes the tone clear.
